answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit bids, with one bid-weight unit per token locked. Splitting a stake across a thousand identities then creates no extra influence: the attacker must acquire and immobilize the same total capital, while risking slashing for provable fraud. A river of opal tokens does not make a cheap mirror army; the binding cost is capital tied up and exposed, not the number of names created.
